note: Promotion to the tracked schema (roadmap Phase 1 backfill). Track groups follow the (XX) prefixes already embedded in the source theme names. Empty fields (track, code, level, description) are filled; authored transfer_check values replace ONLY the two known generic placeholder sentences — real source checks are never overwritten (guard in tools/normalize_blocks.py).

themes.description: Tracing your own water back — river, well, tank or main — and who keeps it safe along the way.
themes.transfer_check: Trace your own tap or well water to its actual source and draw the path, naming who safeguards each stage.

themes.description: The path of used water from your drain — sewer, septic or ground — and your household's end of that bargain.
themes.transfer_check: Trace your own wastewater to its actual destination — works, tank or ground — and state your household's two protective behaviours.

themes.theme: When the water is not safe (WA)
themes.description: The signs and notices of unsafe water, and the boil, filter and treat options ranked by what they remove.
themes.transfer_check: Demonstrate one correct treatment method — boil, filter or disinfect — and match three contamination types to the method that removes each.

themes.description: Moving and storing water without contaminating it — clean containers, covered storage and the ladle rule.
themes.transfer_check: Collect, carry and store water for one day's household use without contaminating it, narrating the rules you followed.

themes.description: Flooding where you live — where it comes from, what it touches first, and the household moves before and after.
themes.transfer_check: Read your address's flood exposure from official maps and state the household action sequence at three warning lead times.

themes.description: Drought and scarcity — rationing a household honestly, and the uses that go first.
themes.transfer_check: Ration a real or simulated day on a fixed water budget, allocating by priority and logging where every litre went.

themes.description: The simple tests and observations that say something real about water, and reading an official quality report.
themes.transfer_check: Perform one simple water test or observation on a real source and correctly read an official quality report for your supply.

themes.description: Finding a leak with the meter-still test, the repairs within reach, and what a slow drip costs over a year.
themes.transfer_check: Run the meter-still leak test on a real dwelling and repair or precisely specify one leak found, with its yearly cost computed.

themes.description: What water costs where you live — the bill, the tariff, the subsidy — and using the price to find the waste.
themes.transfer_check: Read one real water bill against the meter and tariff, and identify the household's most expensive water habit with figures.

themes.description: Wells, standpipes and irrigation shared by many — the rules, rotas and disputes of a common source.
themes.transfer_check: Document the rules of one real shared water source — who may take, when, who maintains — and how one past dispute was settled.

themes.theme: What this ground is made of (LD)
themes.description: Reading your local soil and rock — what drains, what slips, what grows — from a hole you dug yourself.
themes.transfer_check: Dig or expose one real soil profile, classify what you find, and state what it means for drainage and growing.

themes.theme: Who owns the ground you stand on (LD)
themes.description: Titles, tenancies and commons — the ownership map of your own area and where it is recorded.
themes.transfer_check: Find the recorded ownership of one real parcel through the official registry and explain the record to somebody else.

themes.description: Erosion and degradation — the signs of ground leaving, and the plantings and barriers that hold it.
themes.transfer_check: Survey one real site for erosion signs and install or specify the planting or barrier that would hold it.

themes.description: Preparing a bed, choosing what suits the soil and season, and tending one deliberate crop to harvest.
themes.transfer_check: Prepare a bed, plant a crop suited to your soil and season, and tend it to harvest with a care log.

themes.description: Vacant lots and margins — who actually owns them, and the lawful routes to putting them to use.
themes.transfer_check: Identify one real vacant parcel, find its actual owner through records, and outline the lawful route to a community use.

themes.description: Making a real map of a real place — boundaries, water, slopes, uses — accurate enough for someone else to follow.
themes.transfer_check: Produce a real map of one place — boundaries, water, slope, uses — accurate enough for a stranger to navigate by.

themes.description: The land rules that bind where you live — zoning, building, clearing — and where a decision can be looked up.
themes.transfer_check: Look up the actual rules governing one real land question where you live and state what is allowed, forbidden and permitted-with-approval.

themes.description: Taking one degraded patch back — clearing, soil, planting, protection — and keeping it alive past the first season.
themes.transfer_check: Take one small degraded patch through clearing, soil work and planting, and keep it alive past a season with evidence.

themes.description: Surveying the species of one real place, and what their presence or absence says about its health.
themes.transfer_check: Conduct a species survey of one real place and interpret what two presences or absences say about its health.

themes.description: Sealed ground, drains and heat — what paving does to water and temperature, and the green that repairs it.
themes.transfer_check: Map sealed and green ground on one real block and measure or estimate the difference it makes to runoff or heat.

themes.description: Collecting older residents' accounts of past seasons and comparing them honestly to the record.
themes.transfer_check: Record one elder's account of past seasons and check two of its specifics against the instrumental record, reporting honestly.

themes.description: A simple weather log kept properly — instrument, time, place — until it becomes data.
themes.transfer_check: Keep a daily weather log — instrument, time, place — for two weeks and present it as usable data.

themes.description: Extreme heat where you live — who it endangers, the hours that matter, and cooling a body and a room.
themes.transfer_check: Write and rehearse a heat-day plan for a real household naming the dangerous hours, the cooling method and the person checked on.

themes.description: Cold snaps — the household risks from pipes to lungs, and protecting the people heating one room.
themes.transfer_check: Prepare a real dwelling and household for a cold snap against a checklist — pipes, heating, the one warm room — and demonstrate it.

themes.description: Shifting rains and growing seasons — reading the change in local planting, prices and water.
themes.transfer_check: Document one local seasonal shift — planting date, rain arrival, price curve — from two independent local sources.

themes.description: The storms your region actually gets, their warning signs, and the before-during-after sequence for a household.
themes.transfer_check: Run the before-during-after sequence for your region's storm type in a household drill, with the kit and refuge demonstrated.

themes.description: What is in the air you breathe — smoke, dust, exhaust — reading an air quality index and acting on a bad day.
themes.transfer_check: Read today's actual air quality for your location, name its dominant source, and state the action the level calls for.

themes.description: Probability, timing and range in a real forecast — what it promises, what it cannot, and planning with it.
themes.transfer_check: Take one real multi-day forecast, explain its probabilities and limits, and make one genuine plan that uses it correctly.

themes.description: The cheap adaptations first — shade, storage, drainage, timing — ranked by cost against protection.
themes.transfer_check: Rank three low-cost adaptations for a real dwelling by cost against protection, and implement the first.

themes.description: Disagreeing about climate with evidence and respect — the claims, the sources, and the difference between the two.
themes.transfer_check: Hold a structured disagreement on one climate claim using cited evidence on both sides, and state what would change your mind.

themes.description: Your own electricity traced to its sources — the plants, lines and fuels behind the local socket.
themes.transfer_check: Trace your own electricity to its actual generation mix from published data and present the chain socket-to-source.

themes.description: Running the essentials through an outage — light, food, phones — safely and in the right order.
themes.transfer_check: Run a two-hour household blackout drill covering light, one hot meal and phone charging, every method used safely.

themes.theme: Reading a meter and a bill (EN)
themes.description: The kilowatt-hour as the unit you buy — reading your meter and reconciling it with the bill.
themes.transfer_check: Read your real meter on two dates, compute the kilowatt-hours used, and reconcile them against the bill.

themes.description: Finding where warmth leaves a dwelling and the sealing and insulation that pay for themselves first.
themes.transfer_check: Survey a real dwelling for heat loss and implement or specify the two cheapest effective fixes, payback estimated.

themes.description: The fuels people cook with — their cost, smoke and danger — and the safest option a household can reach.
themes.transfer_check: Compare the real cooking fuels available to your household on cost, smoke and safety, and demonstrate the safest setup.

themes.theme: Sun and wind on this site (EN)
themes.description: Reading one real site for solar and wind potential — orientation, shading, exposure — before believing a brochure.
themes.transfer_check: Assess one real site's solar or wind potential — orientation, shading, exposure — and deliver a defensible yes/no with reasons.

themes.description: Batteries and other stores — what they hold, what they cost, and matching a store to a real need.
themes.transfer_check: Size a battery or store for one named real need from actual wattages, and show the arithmetic.

themes.description: The energy embedded in objects and food — why making, moving and wasting things is an energy question.
themes.transfer_check: Estimate the embedded energy of one everyday object from its materials and transport, and present the chain.

themes.description: The jobs that keep power flowing — lines, plants, meters — and the training routes into them locally.
themes.transfer_check: Map two real local routes into energy work — the roles, the training, the entry requirements — from actual providers.

themes.description: Tariffs, subsidies and siting — where energy decisions are made near you and how a resident is heard.
themes.transfer_check: Identify where one real energy decision near you is made — tariff, siting, subsidy — and submit or draft a resident's input to it.

themes.description: The ranked, evidenced list of what can actually happen at your address — flood, storm, fire, slide.
themes.transfer_check: Build the ranked, evidenced hazard list for your own address from official maps and records.

themes.description: One written plan a household has rehearsed — contacts, rally points, kit and the leave triggers.
themes.transfer_check: Write the household emergency plan — contacts, rally points, kit, leave triggers — and run its drill with the real occupants.

themes.description: Reading a building's weak points against local hazards — roof, openings, exits — and the fixes in reach.
themes.transfer_check: Assess one real building's weak points against your local hazards and fix or specify the two worst, with photos.

themes.description: The official warning channels where you live, tested on your own devices, and what each level demands.
themes.transfer_check: Verify every official warning channel for your area on your own devices, tested, and state what each alert level demands.

themes.description: Water, food, light, warmth and information for three days on your own shelf.
themes.transfer_check: Assemble or audit a real 72-hour kit for your household's actual members and gaps found made good.

themes.description: Re-entry done safely — structure, power, contamination — and the documentation that starts recovery.
themes.transfer_check: Walk a staged or documented re-entry — structure, power, contamination checks in order — and start the claim documentation.

themes.theme: Insurance and what it does not cover (RS)
themes.description: Reading a policy for the hazard exclusions, and the public help that exists where insurance does not.
themes.transfer_check: Read one real policy against your hazard list and report every exclusion that matters, with the public backstops named.

themes.description: Building back against the next event — elevation, materials, siting — instead of repeating the loss.
themes.transfer_check: For one real or documented damaged dwelling, specify the build-back changes that beat the next event, roughly costed.

themes.description: Why the same event lands unequally — age, money, mobility, location — and planning for the street, not just the house.
themes.transfer_check: Map, with consent, the vulnerable households on one street and agree the check-in protocol that activates in an event.

themes.description: The event log — what happened, when, what worked — kept so the next response starts smarter.
themes.transfer_check: Write the event log of one real drill or incident — what happened, when, what worked — and change one plan because of it.
